label: text

label: text
text:
An increase in the capital of half a million dollars—allotted to one shareholder—was voted at an extraordinary general meeting of the Hongkong and Territorial Estates, Ltd., held this morning at the office of Messrs. Shewan, Tomes & Co. (general managers).
Mr. R. G. Shewan presided. Members of the consulting committee present were Messrs.—F. M. Raymond, J. Scott Harston,

label: text
text: Shareholders attending included Messrs: A. L. Shields, I. W. Shewan, R. Fairnant, D. W. Murnton, A. Keith, H. Dreyer, J. Toppin, A. A. Botelhe

label: text
text: After Mr. A. Brian (manager and see letary) had read the notice, the chairman said:—

label: text
text: "Gentlemen.—The object of the Resolutions in the Notice just rends is simply to raise further Working Capital. This would not have been necessary, had the Final Calls on Shares been fully met, but I am sorry to say that about $296,250 is still outstanding."

label: text
text: "Although we are taking steps to secure payment of this amount as far as possible, the circumstances obtaining at the present time are such as to render this a matter of difficulty."

label: text
text: "In consequence of the foregoing we must realise further capital, and we propose to make an issue of fresh capital to the extent of $500,000 in (consolidative Preferred shares, bearing interest at seven per cent. (7%)). We do not propose to offer these shares to shareholders generally because circumstances have shown that at the present time the offer would not be accepted to any extent worth considering, while the circulation of it would waste a great deal of time. We have therefore approached the largest shareholder who is disposed to take up the shares, and we think the interests of the company will be best served by allotting them to him."

label: text
text: The two "ordinary" revolutions were the pull separately, as follow:—

label: text
text: 1. The capital of the Company be increased by the creation of 50,000 new shares of $10,000 each to be exhaled. Preference Shares to which there shall be attached the special rights and privileges following that is to say:

label: text

label: text

label: text

The activities of the local movement as part of the parent body known as the Mothers' Union were outlined at a meeting at Government House on Tuesday.
Meetings in connection with it are held at the Helena May Institute on alternative Tuesday afternoons and for the purpose of re-awakening interest in the discussions and general activities of the branch the meeting was held at Government House at the invitation of Lady Cecil Clementi.
Mrs. M. J. Noll, the Honorary local secretary, 165, the Peak, spoke on the activities of the branch here, also Mrs. Duppy, Diocesan President, Mrs. Warren and the Bishop of Victoria and Lady Clementi added a few words as Diocesan Patron, Rev. G. R. Lindsay spoke of the growth of the Kowloon branch.

label: doc_title
text: BANDIT ATTACK

label: text
text:
AMEPICAN MISSIONARY
IN FUKIEN

label: text
text: SERVANT SERIOUSLY WOUNDED

label: text
text: From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Word has just been received that the Rev. Henry A. Poppen, an American missionary of the Reformed Church in America, with his family was attacked by bandits while en route from Amoy to his station, Lungyenchow, in the interior of South Fukien. The bandits shot one of Mr. Poppen's servants, inflicting a serious wound, and then took charge of all baggage.

label: text
text: Amoy, Jan. 17.

label: text
text: Almost everything of value was taken including clothes, money, and jewellery. After the baggage had been completely runsacked, the bandits were satisfied and the missionaries were allowed to proceed to their destination.

label: text
text: Mr. Poppen, with his wife and two children, had just returned to China from furlough. As their station is rather difficult to reach, supplies for some months to come were being carried along to Lungvenchoy. Most of these were taken along with other things.

label: paragraph_title
text: EXPENSIVE "FIND."

label: text
text:
MARINE
AGENT AND OLD
SHIP

label: text
text: ARMS IN HOUSE.

label: text
text:
A "find" of arms on a vessel which he as marine dealer had bought to break up led to the appearance at the Central Magistracy this morning of the master of the Sang Loong firm.
The weapons were found in his house as a result of information given to the police.

label: text
text: Mr. Leo d'Almada's defence for the man was that the weapons had been placed out of the children's way and there never had been intention to use them. They had lain there since 1923 when the ship was bought.

label: text
text: The Police evidence was that the arms were not much good. A fine of $50 was imposed.

label: doc_title
text: THE NEXT ADVANCE.

label: text
text: LOOKED FOR FROM CANTON.

label: text
text: The Hofm-Colónial Secretary has released the following for publication:—

label: text
text: His Excellency the Governor soon after his arrival, following a gesture of friendship in a speech at the University, took advantage of the presence in the Colony of a merchant delegation from Canton to announce that the Government would be willing to appoint a strong deputation of influential merchants to visit Canton to initiate discussions with a view to a settlement, provided that the Canton Government would appoint delegates of equal standing and responsibility to meet them. The proposal was conveyed to the Canton Government, and was met with the reply that

label: text
text: ) the merchants would also elect one prominent merchant to be a member of the delegation: this would probably be the Chairman of the Canton General Chamber of Commerce.

label: text
text: a) the strikers would elect three members of their Committee to be delegates with full powers to negotiate, one of them almost certainly being the Chairman of the Strike Committee.

label: text
text: (c) other members of the Strike Committee, probably six, and perhaps one or two additional merchants, would be present at the negotiations to switch the proceedings: and

label: text
text: (d) that a minor Cantonese official could be attached to the delegation as Secretary.

label: text
text: This reply failed to respond to the spirit in which the suggestion of the Hongkong Government had been made, and it was felt that no useful purpose would be served by a conference between a delegation not appointed by the Canton. Government, and the gentlemen whom the Canton Government had nominated. Efforts were therefore made by Hongkong to open negotiations upon other lines.

label: text
text: Other Lines.

label: text
text: 2. These efforts took the form of a suggestion that Hongkong officials of high standing should be added to the Colony's delegation, and that the Canton Government should take similar action on their part; both delegations to be armed with full powers from their respective Governments for the settlement of all outstanding questions. The Canton Government, however, took the attitude that it could only appoint representatives to act as mediators; and the position that the Hongkong Government should appoint a delegation including officials as plenipotentiary delegates, appearing as principals vis-à-vis the Canton delegation described above, whereas Canton would only appoint officers "to mediate," was one that could not be accepted.

label: text
text:
This effort therefore also failed.
3. An interchange of visits between important officials of Hongkong and Canton then took place, and discussions were held on the lines of separating the “political” and so-called “economic” questions at issue. It was considered that negotiation on the “economic” side could best be con-

label: text
text: ducted by Chinese business men, and on the understanding so reached, the Hongkong Government acquiesced in the suggestion for a visit to Canton by a delegation of eight prominent Chinese appointed by the Chinese Community. It was understood that this delegation would deal directly with the Strike Committee, and would negotiate with them the "economic" questions, namely, strike pay and compensation for loss of employment, leaving all "political" questions for later consideration between the two Governments; the Strike and the Boycott to cease on the settlement of the "economic" questions.

label: text
text: On reaching Canton, however, on December 30, the delegation of eight found that no assistance could be looked for from the Canton Government towards meeting the Strike Committee and discussing the "economic" terms with them unless they were also prepared to discuss and settle with the Strike Committee at the same time "political" terms. For this the delegation clearly could have no authority; its members thoroughly explored every possible avenue for negotiation, and left no doubt of their sincerity, but the visit proved entirely fruitless, and they returned to the Colony on January 2.

label: text
text: The Hongkong Government is prepared at any time to resume negotiations, but in the circumstances detailed cannot see that any useful purpose will be served by any further delegation to Cantons at the present time, and it now remains for the Canton Government on its side to give evidence of sincerity by making the next advance.

label: paragraph_title
text: JAPAN'S CONSUL

label: text
text: YESTERDAY'S PLEASANT GATHERING.

label: text
text: The Japanese Consul-General, Mr. Y. Murakami, gave a tiffin party at the Hongkong Hotel yesterday. The gathering was quite informal, and was held in Mr. Murakami's words, "to strengthen old friendships and to make new ones."

label: text
text: Among those present were the Colonial Secretary, Mr. E. R. Hallifax; the Colonial Treasurer, Mr. C. McI. Messenger; the Director of Public Works, Mr. H. T. Creasy; the Captain Superintendent of Police, Mr. P. J. Wodehouse; the Secretary for Chinese Affairs, Mr. D. W. Trattman; the Director of Education, Mr. A. E. Wood; Lieutenant-Commander G. F. Hole, Mr. R. Ponsonby, Mr. J. Abe, Mr. O. T. Breakspear, Mr. A. Hicks, Mr. S. Kinoshita, Mr. B. Wylie, Mr. Y. Tsutsumi, Mr. C. M. McDonald, Mr. S. Okubo, Mr. W. Jackson, and Mr. T. Yamazaki. At the conclusion of tiffin Mr. Murakami, after expressing the pleasure it gave him to entertain his guests, referred to the friendship that had existed for so long between Great Britain and Japan and trusted that it might always continue. Mr. E. R. Hallifax and Mr. Ponsonby Fane returned thanks on behalf of the visitors for the hospitality accorded them and reciprocated the good wishes of the host.
